limitations: The RM service loop may exit on a stuck interrupt after a void dispatch; the returned NV_OK is not proof that every pending engine drained.

The Linux ISR invokes RM fault-buffer handling before the UVM top-half callback. The UVM suspend flag and UVM top-half use interrupts_lock, but these source paths do not establish that suspend waits for an in-flight Linux RM interrupt handler.

The procfs PM ordering applies only to its full-depth successful path: MODESET returns before channel preemption or UVM suspend, UVM depth returns after UVM and before per-device GPU suspend, and the Linux PCI suspend callback invokes nvidia_suspend directly. The audit does not cover generic Linux noirq IRQ suspension.
The procfs depth-selection and suspend-dispatch predicates fail closed if either inspected function contains a preprocessor directive; no build-specific preprocessor branches are inferred.
The RM interrupt service path consumes RM software-shadow faults and notifies clients after the hardware-buffer copy step; source inspection does not prove its runtime completion or PM safety.

The GV100 generated-HAL result is conditional: the source assigns the GV100 copier for the VF RM variant when the chip-HAL mask for T234D/T264D does not match. This source branch alone does not establish the runtime HAL selection for a particular physical GPU.
The GET-pointer publication-order fact applies only to the nonempty-copy path. When totalCount is zero, GV100 rewrites the cached GET pointer and exits without a shadow-buffer publication.
No RM call, GPU operation, module load, suspend, concurrent ISR/PM test, or fault-injection test was run.

ordering_assessment.decision: Do not add an RM service call to the candidate suspend path until the in-flight Linux ISR ordering and RM control runtime/error semantics are independently closed.
ordering_assessment.generated_hal_condition: RmVariantHal VF branch AND chipHal T234D/T264D mask condition false assigns kgmmuCopyMmuFaults_GV100; this is source-conditional and not a physical-device selection result.

hardware_fault_buffer_paths.empty_total_count: rewrites cached GET and exits without shadow publication
hardware_fault_buffer_paths.nonempty_total_count: copies to shadow queue, clears packets, fences, sets fatalFaultIntrPending, fences, then advances GET

ordering_assessment.inference: A UVM suspend racing an already-running Linux ISR is not ruled out by the UVM interrupts_lock alone because the RM fault-copy call precedes UVM top-half entry. Whether another Linux/RM PM barrier excludes that interleaving is unknown.

pm_irq_quiescence.decision: Keep the UVM non-replayable drain patch as an unqualified candidate; do not claim producer quiescence or merge/install it until the in-flight ISR ordering is resolved and tested.
pm_irq_quiescence.inference: The RM interrupt gate is not itself an explicit Linux synchronize_irq/free_irq join. Because nvidia_isr copies RM faults before entering the UVM top half, a handler that already passed the GV100 interrupt-state check is not proven complete by the source-visible PM wrapper sequence. The UVM interrupts_lock protects UVM top-half state, not that earlier RM copy.
pm_irq_quiescence.source_observation: On the procfs full-depth success path, nv_suspend_devices preempts user channels, invokes UVM suspend, then calls per-device nvidia_suspend. MODESET depth returns before preemption/UVM; UVM depth returns after UVM and before per-device suspend. The Linux PCI callback calls nvidia_suspend directly. Its RM wrapper stores INTERRUPT_TYPE_DISABLED before gpuEnterStandby/Hibernate. intrSetIntrEn_IMPL assigns the RM software field; the GV100 fault copier returns early when that field reads disabled.

ordering_assessment.source_observation: nvidia_isr calls rm_gpu_handle_mmu_faults before nv_uvm_event_interrupt; the physical non-GSP helper dispatches kgmmuCopyMmuFaults_HAL. In the generated HAL block, the VF RM variant uses the GV100 copier on the else branch of the T234D/T264D chip-HAL mask test; other branches assign different copiers.
